name: The Town's Levy
about: The guilds of a rich town offer the King its levy for his next campaign, six hundred men and their pikes, if he gives them a charter that takes them out from under their lord. Take the men and the lord turns on you. Refuse and the town shuts its gates, and a rival lord offers it his protection and its men his banner.
title: The Levy of {town}

create.name: Master {first} Weaver
create.memory: My father marched in this town's levy for the lord and came home without his legs.

goal.text: A charter for the guilds, under the King's seal, and the town's levy marching under the King's banner

beats.speaker: master
beats.text: The guild wardens of {town} come to Kingsmere with a muster roll: six hundred men, armed at the town's cost, to march in the King's next campaign. Their price is a charter, a council of their own, and their levy answering to the King instead of {lord}.

court.text: {lord} of {lord.house} followed them to court: "Those are my men, Your Grace. My father raised that levy. Take it from me and you can take my sword too, because I won't be using it for you."

options.label: Take the levy, and seal {town}'s charter
options.hint: {lord.houseName} −25 · six hundred pikes for the King's campaign
options.result: The King seals {town}'s charter. Six hundred men drill in the square under the royal banner, and {lord} rides past them without a word.

options.label: Refuse: {town}'s levy is its lord's
options.result: The roll goes back unsealed. On the road home the wardens stop talking about the King's war and start talking about their gates.

options.label: Let {lord} deal with them
options.result: The King hands the muster roll to {lord}, who folds it small and tucks it in {lord.his} boot.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {town}'s levy drills for the King and stops paying {lord}'s war tax. {lord} counts {lord.his} own host, six hundred men short, and looks at the King's letters.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} says a lord's levy was never the King's to take, and sends knights onto the road into {town} to drag the men back to {lord.his} own muster.

court.text: {lord}: "Those men have stood in my ranks for three generations, Your Grace. I'll have them back, or your crown will answer for it."

options.label: Pay {lord} for the lost levy (300 gold)
options.result: The King buys {lord}'s right to the levy for a price {lord.he} pretends is an insult.

options.label: The charter stands: call off the knights
options.result: Royal heralds read the charter out at the crossroads. {lord}'s knights hear it, and keep riding.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} deals with it: the warden who carried the muster roll hangs from {town}'s market cross. {master} cuts him down at night, and the levy swears an oath over the body.

beats.speaker: master
beats.text: {town} won't send a single man to {lord}'s muster. The forges stop making {lord.his} spearheads, the war tax isn't paid, and {lord}'s host is the first to feel it.

court.text: {lord}: "They're starving my host to make a point, Your Grace. Send me men and I'll make a point of my own."

options.label: Take the levy and seal the charter after all
options.hint: {lord.houseName} −25 · six hundred pikes for the King
options.result: The King seals {town}'s charter. The forges start again by noon, making royal spearheads.

options.label: Send soldiers to drive the men to {lord}'s muster
options.result: Pikemen kick in the guild-hall doors of {town}. They find the pikes, and nobody to carry them.

options.label: Quietly pay off the guild masters (200 gold)
options.hint: the men go back to {lord} · the anger stays
options.result: Purses go to the right houses at night. The levy falls in behind {lord}'s banner by the end of the week, and nobody admits taking anything.

beats.speaker: master
beats.text: {town} shuts its gates on {lord}, mans its own walls with its own levy, and sends riders to every lord who might want six hundred pikes. {protector} answers first.

court.text: {protector} of {protector.house}: "{town}'s levy has asked to march under my banner, Your Grace. I'd rather it marched under yours. Will you take it, or shall I?"

options.label: Take {town} and its levy under the crown
options.hint: {lord.houseName} −35 · six hundred pikes for the King · every town watches
options.result: The King's banner goes up over {town}'s gate beside the guilds' own. The levy marches out to join the royal host. {lord} isn't there to see it.

options.label: Storm the gates and end it

die.how: They broke our gates and I died in the guild-hall door.

options.result: {lord}'s knights go over {town}'s walls with the King's leave.

options.label: Give {town} and its levy to {protector}
options.result: {town} opens its gates to {protector}'s banner. Its levy swears to a lord who promises to leave its charter alone.

beats.speaker: protector
beats.text: One market town after another shuts its gates and musters its own levy. {protector} rides at the head of their militias toward Kingsmere, promising every one of them a charter.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} won't be a lord without a levy. {lord.He} calls up the banners {lord.he} has left against a King who steals a lord's men, and marches.

beats.speaker: master
beats.text: {town}'s levy marches under the King's banner now. Its council meets in the old wool hall, and three other towns have sent wardens to ask what their men would fetch.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {town}'s levy stands in {lord}'s ranks again. Nobody talks about the charter, and the guild-hall's founding stone is turned to face the wall.
